questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make friends at work
Why talking to strangers can be good for us
How many words there are in English
Why introverts prefer to be alone
questions.why: Neil says they are looking at how talking to strangers might be good for you.

questions.q: How does Georgina feel about starting a conversation with a stranger?
options: She does it every day
She thinks it is rude
She is unsure what she would talk about
She is too shy to talk to anyone
questions.why: She asks, 'if you don't know them, what are you going to start talking about?'

questions.q: Why do we rarely talk to strangers, according to the presenters?
options: We fear it would feel awkward for both people
We are usually in too much of a hurry
It is not polite in most countries
We are always looking at our phones
questions.why: Georgina says we fear it would make us both feel uncomfortable or awkward.

questions.q: According to Gillian Sandstrom, what does the 'negative voice in our head' do?
options: Tells us the other person is bored and wants to leave
Makes us talk too much and forget to listen to others
Warns us that strangers could be dangerous to talk to
Criticises what we said and makes us doubt ourselves
questions.why: It tells us 'I shouldn't have said that' and 'I said that story better last time'.

questions.q: What does Gillian Sandstrom say the other person often thinks after the conversation?
options: That the chat was a waste of time
That the speaker was amazing
That they didn't understand the speaker
That they want to leave quickly
questions.why: She says they think, 'wow, that person was amazing.'

questions.q: What did the University of Chicago research find?
options: Commuters on trains are the unhappiest people in the city
Strangers usually refuse to talk when someone starts chatting
We expect less joy from chatting to strangers than we get
Only long conversations with friends improve our wellbeing
questions.why: It found we underestimate the positive impact, and a chat may leave you happier than you'd think.

questions.q: According to Gillian Sandstrom's research, what are two effects of chatting to strangers?
options: A better mood and feeling more connected
Better sleep and more energy
More confidence and a better job
Less stress and better memory
questions.why: She says it's good for your mood and makes people feel more connected to each other.

options: They should avoid talking to strangers
They never enjoy conversations
They were not included in the experiments
Talking to others can make them happier too
questions.why: Neil says even introverts can become happier by talking to others, experiments show.
